name: MongoDB Data Architecture & Aggregations Track
description: Master NoSQL document modeling, BSON data types, CRUD operations, Aggregation Pipelines, compound indexing, transactions, and enterprise database engineering.
whatYouLearn: Execute complex CRUD operations with query operators ($gt, $in, $elemMatch)
Optimize query performance using single-field and compound Indexes
Model relationships using embedding vs referencing patterns
Build an Inventory Management System Database

exercises.title: BSON Documents & Collection Insertions (insertOne, insertMany)
exercises.description: Insert single and bulk BSON documents into MongoDB collections.
exercises.theory: MongoDB stores data records as BSON (Binary JSON) documents inside collections. insertOne inserts one document, while insertMany inserts arrays of documents.
exercises.objective: Insert single and array document payloads into a products collection.
exercises.initialCode: // Execute MongoDB insertOne and insertMany operations
requirements: Use db.collection.insertOne() with document payload
Use db.collection.insertMany() with document array
hints: MongoDB automatically generates a unique _id ObjectId if not supplied

exercises.title: Querying Documents (find, findOne & Projection)
exercises.description: Query documents with equality matches, projections, and pagination (limit, skip).
exercises.theory: find(query, projection) retrieves documents. Projections ({ name: 1, _id: 0 }) specify which fields to return.
exercises.objective: Find electronics products excluding _id from output.
requirements: Query category: 'Electronics'
Use projection { name: 1, price: 1, _id: 0 }
Chain .sort({ price: -1 }) and .limit(5)
hints: 1 includes a field in projection; 0 excludes a field

exercises.title: Comparison Query Operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $in)
exercises.description: Filter documents using comparison query operators.
exercises.theory: Comparison operators include $eq (equal), $ne (not equal), $gt (greater than), $gte (greater than or equal), $lt, $lte, and $in (matches array values).
exercises.objective: Query products priced between $20 and $100 in specified categories.
requirements: Use $gte and $lte price bounds
Use $in operator for category array match
hints: $in takes an array of values to match against

exercises.title: Logical Query Operators ($and, $or, $nor, $not)
exercises.description: Combine complex filtering conditions using logical query operators.
exercises.theory: Logical operators ($or, $and, $nor, $not) combine multiple clause expressions.
exercises.objective: Query items matching either category or discount conditions.
requirements: Use $or operator containing two filter clauses
Use $and for stock validation
hints: $or takes an array of query condition objects

exercises.title: Update Operators ($set, $unset, $inc)
exercises.description: Update document fields using atomic update operators.
exercises.theory: updateOne and updateMany require atomic update operators ($set modifies fields, $unset removes fields, $inc increments numerical values).
exercises.objective: Increment stock quantity and update status on matching items.
requirements: Use $inc to increment stockCount by 10
Use $set to update lastRestocked timestamp and inStock boolean
hints: Always use atomic operators like $set inside update documents to avoid overwriting entire documents

exercises.title: Array Update Operators ($push, $pull, $addToSet)
exercises.description: Manipulate nested document arrays atomically.
exercises.theory: $push adds elements to an array, $pull removes matching elements, and $addToSet adds elements only if they do not already exist (unique set behavior).
exercises.objective: Add unique tags to a product document array.
requirements: Use $addToSet operator with $each modifier
Prevent duplicate tag strings from being added
hints: $addToSet prevents duplicate array values; $each allows adding multiple array items at once

exercises.title: Deletion & Bulk Operations (deleteOne, deleteMany, bulkWrite)
exercises.description: Delete records safely and execute high-throughput bulk write operations.
exercises.theory: deleteOne and deleteMany remove documents matching query criteria. bulkWrite executes ordered or unordered batch operations.
exercises.objective: Delete out-of-stock items and run a bulkWrite operations batch.
requirements: Delete items with inStock: false and stockCount: 0
Execute bulkWrite containing insertOne and updateOne operations
hints: deleteMany({}) without query filter deletes all documents in collection

exercises.title: Aggregation Pipeline Basics ($match, $project)
exercises.description: Build multi-stage aggregation pipelines to filter and reshape documents.
exercises.theory: The Aggregation Framework processes documents through ordered pipeline stages. $match filters documents; $project reshapes document fields.
exercises.objective: Build a 2-stage aggregation pipeline with $match and $project.
requirements: Stage 1: $match for category: 'Electronics' and inStock: true
Stage 2: $project to rename productName and format price string
hints: Prefix field names with $ (e.g. '$price') inside aggregation expressions to reference field values

exercises.title: Aggregation Grouping & Accumulators ($group, $sum, $avg)
exercises.description: Group dataset rows and compute aggregate totals, averages, and counts.
exercises.theory: $group stage collapses documents by a specified _id key and computes accumulated values ($sum, $avg, $min, $max).
exercises.objective: Calculate total stock value and average price grouped by category.
requirements: Group by category using _id: '$category'
Compute totalProducts count using $sum: 1
Compute average price with $avg and total value with $multiply
hints: Setting _id: '$category' groups documents by unique category values

exercises.title: Array Aggregations ($unwind, $arrayElemAt)
exercises.description: Deconstruct document arrays into individual stream documents using $unwind.
exercises.theory: $unwind outputs a new document for each element in a target array field, enabling individual array item grouping.
exercises.objective: Unwind product tags array and calculate tag occurrences.
requirements: Stage 1: $unwind: '$tags'
Stage 2: $group by _id: '$tags' and calculate sum count
Stage 3: $sort descending by tagCount
hints: $unwind expands an array containing 3 items into 3 separate documents

exercises.title: Relational Joins with $lookup Stage
exercises.description: Perform left outer joins between collections using the $lookup aggregation stage.
exercises.theory: $lookup performs relational joins between collections matching localField with foreignField from another collection.
exercises.objective: Join order documents with customer profile details.
requirements: Use $lookup with from: 'users', localField: 'userId', foreignField: '_id', as: 'customerDetails'
Unwind joined customerDetails array
Project clean order and customer payload
hints: $lookup returns joined matches as an array on the target specified in 'as'

exercises.title: Single-Field & Compound Indexes
exercises.description: Create single-field, compound, and unique indexes using createIndex().
exercises.theory: Indexes speed up read query performance by maintaining an ordered data structure. Compound indexes optimize queries matching multiple fields.
exercises.objective: Create unique single-field index on email and compound index on category/price.
requirements: Create unique index on users.email
Create compound index on products { category: 1, price: -1 }
hints: 1 specifies ascending index order; -1 specifies descending index order

exercises.title: Text Indexes & Full-Text Search ($text, $search)
exercises.description: Create full-text search indexes and query text using $text and $search.
exercises.theory: Text indexes enable searching for words within string fields without requiring exact string or regex matches.
exercises.objective: Create a text index on product title/description and execute text search.
requirements: Create text index on name and description fields
Query using $text: { $search: '...' }
Project and sort by textScore metadata
hints: Text search ranks documents using textScore relevance metadata

exercises.title: Geospatial Indexing & Location Queries ($near, $geoWithin)
exercises.description: Store GeoJSON Point data and query locations using 2dsphere indexes.
exercises.theory: 2dsphere indexes query GeoJSON point objects on a spherical earth model using operators like $near and $maxDistance.
exercises.objective: Query stores within 5000 meters of a GeoJSON coordinate.
requirements: Create 2dsphere index on location field
Query using $near and $geometry GeoJSON Point coordinates
Specify $maxDistance in meters
hints: GeoJSON coordinates order is ALWAYS [longitude, latitude]

exercises.title: Schema Validation Rules ($jsonSchema)
exercises.description: Enforce collection data integrity using native $jsonSchema validation rules.
exercises.theory: MongoDB supports collection-level JSON Schema validation to enforce required fields, data types, and value constraints upon insertion/update.
exercises.objective: Create a users collection with strict $jsonSchema validation.
requirements: Use db.createCollection with validator option
Define required fields array
Define properties with bsonType, pattern, and enum rules
hints: Insertions breaking validator rules throw a MongoServerError validation error

exercises.title: Data Modeling: Embedded vs Referenced Documents
exercises.description: Model 1-to-Few (embedding) vs 1-to-Many / Many-to-Many (referencing) relationships.
exercises.theory: Embed child data when data is accessed together and bounded. Use references (ObjectId pointers) for large, unbounded 1-to-Many relationships.
exercises.objective: Model a user profile with embedded addresses and referenced order IDs.
exercises.initialCode: // Insert document with embedded and referenced data structures
requirements: Embed address object array directly inside user document
Store referenced ObjectId array for orders
hints: Embedded documents save extra $lookup query operations

exercises.title: Multi-Document ACID Transactions
exercises.description: Execute atomic multi-document ACID transactions using sessions.
exercises.theory: Sessions support multi-document ACID transactions across replica sets, guaranteeing all updates commit together or roll back on error.
exercises.objective: Execute a bank transfer multi-document transaction session.
requirements: Start session with startSession() and startTransaction()
Execute multi-document updates passing session context
Commit with commitTransaction() and rollback with abortTransaction()
hints: Always call session.endSession() in finally block

exercises.title: GridFS Storage for Large Files
exercises.description: Store and retrieve files larger than 16MB BSON limit using GridFS buckets.
exercises.theory: GridFS divides files into 255KB chunks stored in fs.chunks and file metadata in fs.files when assets exceed the 16MB document size limit.
exercises.objective: Inspect GridFS chunks and files collections structure.
requirements: Find file record in fs.files collection
Count chunk references in fs.chunks collection matching files_id
hints: GridFS automatically handles splitting and stitching binary streams

exercises.title: Database Profiling & Query Explain (explain('executionStats'))
exercises.description: Analyze query performance and index usage using the .explain() executionStats plan.
exercises.theory: explain('executionStats') displays execution plan details (nReturned, totalKeysExamined, totalDocsExamined, stage: 'IXSCAN' vs 'COLLSCAN').
exercises.objective: Analyze query execution plan using explain('executionStats').
requirements: Chain .explain('executionStats') on find query
Inspect winningPlan.stage and totalDocsExamined
hints: Stage 'IXSCAN' indicates index scan, while 'COLLSCAN' indicates inefficient full collection scan

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Inventory Management Database Architecture
exercises.description: Engineer a complete NoSQL Inventory Management Database featuring Schema Validation, Compound Indexing, Aggregation Stock Reports, and Relational Joins.
exercises.theory: This capstone exercise synthesizes MongoDB database engineering: Schema Validation, Compound Indexes, Aggregation Pipeline reports, relational $lookup joins, and atomic inventory updates.
exercises.objective: Build a complete Inventory Management Database System script.
requirements: Create inventory_items collection with $jsonSchema validation
Create unique index on SKU and compound index on category/quantity
Run multi-stage aggregation calculating stock counts and total inventory valuation
hints: Combine minimum validation bounds on price/quantity with $group sum valuations

references.title: MongoDB Official Manual
references.description: Official reference manual for MongoDB database operations, aggregations, and driver APIs
